name: Shelf Tramway
description: A network of slow-moving streetcars threading through The Shelf's narrow streets. Most units are converted freight trolleys running on embedded track. They move at walking pace through the densest residential blocks, and that's fine — they're not for speed, they're for hauling groceries, furniture, and people who can't walk far. The drivers know every resident by name.
cost: Φ0.50 per ride, often free (drivers look the other way)
autonomy: Human driver only. The tracks are too narrow and irregular for automation.
armament: None. The driver has a bat.
common_usage: Elderly residents, families with children, cargo hauling within The Shelf. More community institution than transit system.
story_hooks: A tramway driver has been delivering messages between Shelf residents for decades — they know every secret in the neighborhood
The embedded tracks run through a sealed building, and the tram still goes through it on a route that shouldn't exist
